messages:
sophie-support: Hey team — customer (AcmeRide) reporting they can’t finish Google/GitHub OAuth from our hosted login; they hit a state mismatch on callback. Repro steps they gave below.

sophie-support: Steps they tried:
1) Click Sign in with Google on our app (https://acmeride.app/login)
2) Redirect to accounts.google.com with state param that contains extra characters (looks like a mix of percent-encoding and an emoji): state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsImV4cCI6MTc5MDA…%F0%9F%98%8A%2B+
3) Google redirects back to https://app.acmeride.com/auth/callback?code=4/0AY0e-g...&state=eyJhbGci...%F0%9F%98%8A%2B+
4) Our callback handler compares returned state to session and fails with "state mismatch". Customer sees an auth failure and can’t sign in.

jay-customer: We see this consistently on Safari iOS 16 and on some older Android browsers. Works in Chrome desktop. Also seen with GitHub login once, not sure how reproducible.

nilay-frontend: @sophie-support could you paste the raw redirect URL from the browser (if they can reproduce)? wondering if there’s a plus vs space decoding issue or Safari changing the character set.

jay-customer: Here’s the exact redirect we captured: https://app.acmeride.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=eyJh...8A%2B+

ian-eng: Quick theory — our session-stored state is the original base64url string (no percent-encoding), but some browsers/OS combos are double-encoding certain chars (emoji -> %F0%9F%98%8A, plus signs retained vs converted to spaces). When we URL-decode the returned state we might end up with different bytes. Also pkce code_challenge was generated client-side with spaces in the URL? any chance the PKCE verifier mismatch too?

marta-security: Also worth noting: GitHub and Google differ in how they treat + in query params — historically + can be decoded as space if application/x-www-form-urlencoded is applied. Emojis are multi-byte and after percent-encoding they should round-trip, but intermediaries (proxies, CDNs, edge workers) sometimes normalize or re-encode.

devops-bot: deploy 1978880123 started by nilay-frontend — patching callback handler to accept base64url and percent-encoded variants for state (temp hotfix).

nilay-frontend: Repro notes from our end: on Safari iOS, the JS open window flow that sets sessionStorage->state then hits provider sometimes serializes state via encodeURIComponent, then redirect through our CDN (edge worker) which rewrites some query params. I can reproduce locally with this snippet:```js
const s = btoa(JSON.stringify({c:1}))+"+";
const encoded = encodeURIComponent(s);
// simulate redirect path that re-encodes
const twice = encodeURIComponent(encoded);
console.log(decodeURIComponent(decodeURIComponent(twice)) === s); // false on Safari emulation
```

ian-eng: Thanks — that matches. Two actionable items: 1) short-term: make callback tolerant — normalize incoming state by trimming trailing spaces, replace ' ' with '+', attempt base64url decode and fallback to raw compare. 2) longer-term: update our edge worker to preserve query param encoding for known oauth routes and add tests for emoji/plus characters.

marta-security: We should be careful with tolerant compares — don’t accept arbitrary states. Only allow normalization steps that are reversible and still cryptographically safe. Log fallback decode attempts to assist in audits.

jay-customer: Appreciate the quick response. Any ETA on fix? This is blocking a small percentage of users on their production app today.

ian-eng: Hotfix deployed to staging (see deploy 1978880123). Can one of you test with AcmeRide's repro URL? If staging looks good, we can push to prod tonight with a short maintenance window.

nilay-frontend: I tested the staging hotfix against the captured redirect URL — it now accepts the returned state and completes login. Edge case: if state contains trailing '+' followed by a space we normalize to '+' before decode.

marta-security: Added a note to the incident log: we accepted normalized state only when HMAC on the state (we now store HMAC alongside session state's raw value) still verifies. If HMAC fails we reject. That keeps security posture intact.

ian-eng: Follow-ups:
- eng-runtime: add unit tests for decode variants (percent-encoded emoji, plus vs space, double-encoded).
- eng-platform: update edge worker rule to stop re-encoding oauth callback query params for our domains.
- docs: add known-browsers caveat in OAuth troubleshooting with recommended client-side encodeURIComponent usage.

devops-bot: deploy 1978880330 completed to production (hotfix = tolerant-state-compare + logging).

jay-customer: Confirmed with AcmeRide — login now completes on Safari iOS. They’re going to run a small cohort and report back tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :party_parrot:

sophie-support: Closing loop with customer and offering follow-up if they see further failures. Will file a postmortem note if recurrence > 0.1% of logins this week.

ian-eng: Filed ENG-3421 to add tests + edge-worker config change. Marking this resolved for now.

marta-security: Also creating a short KB article for our support docs: "OAuth state: plus signs, emoji, and proxy re-encoding" with recommended client and edge settings.

nilay-frontend: TL;DR: root cause = state param got altered (plus/space and double-encoding) by certain browser+edge combos; fix = tolerant compare + edge rule to preserve encoding + tests.

sophie-support: Thanks all — closing thread.
